title: Epidemiological Profile of Maternal Mortality and the Structure of the Maternal and Perinatal Care Network: An Ecological, Longitudinal Analytical Study
content:
Objective: To analyze the epidemiological profile of maternal mortality and its
relationship with care indicators of the Restructuring and Redesign of the Maternal and
Perinatal Care Network Project between 2010 and 2025. Methods: An observational,
ecological, longitudinal, and analytical epidemiological study was conducted using
aggregated secondary data from the panel of the Restructuring and Redesign of the
Maternal and Perinatal Care Network Project, linked to the Brazilian Obstetric
Observatory. 4,294 maternal deaths registered between 2010 and 2025 were analyzed.
Descriptive analyses, calculation of proportion ratios, 95% confidence intervals,
chi-square tests, odds ratios, and evaluation of the completeness of the information were
performed. Results: A predominance of deaths was observed among white women
(54.0%), mixed-race women (34.1%), and black women (9.5%). Direct maternal deaths
accounted for 56.5% of cases, while 57.7% occurred during the postpartum period up to
42 days after delivery. Most deaths occurred in hospitals (92.4%) and among women who had received prior medical care (73.8%). Only 39.1% of cases were investigated by
Maternal Mortality Committees. Black women were overrepresented in maternal deaths
(OR=1.35; 95% CI: 1.16–1.57). It was estimated that 76.1% of deaths were potentially
preventable. Conclusions: Maternal mortality in São Paulo remains marked by racial
inequities, high preventability, and limitations in death surveillance. Strengthening the
healthcare network, the quality of obstetric care, and information systems is
fundamental to reducing maternal deaths.
